title: The Batch
subtitle: Save it. Revisit it. Make it count.
description: A phone-friendly weekly feed that brings starred Gmail and X bookmarks into one place, with item state and discussion threads that carry over from week to week.
capabilities: Saturday refresh through GitHub Actions
Persistent new, seen, sparred, acted, and dismissed states
Portable JSON context store shared by the feed and a desktop client
note: Write-back is asynchronous: browser changes are exported manually and folded into the next scheduled batch. No private saved items are reproduced here.
problem: Saved links are easy to collect and hard to return to. A weekly feed makes revisiting them intentional instead of another endless inbox.
how: A scheduled GitHub Actions job builds a static feed from a JSON context store. Phone changes are queued locally and exported manually; the next batch folds them back into the store.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The published artifact connects a static phone-friendly feed, a portable context store, and an asynchronous write-back workflow. Private saved items and account configuration are not part of this portfolio.

title: Lineage

description: A local-first workspace that turns GitHub Copilot CLI conversations into a branching knowledge tree. Explore a new direction without losing where an idea came from.
capabilities: Branch from addressable Markdown blocks
Keep parent context without leaking sibling conversations
Own an inspectable, Git-backed vault of Markdown and metadata

problem: A linear agent conversation makes it hard to try another direction without losing the source of an idea or dragging in unrelated branches.
how: FastAPI serves a React interface on localhost. Copilot CLI responses become addressable Markdown blocks; a new branch carries its root-to-fork lineage but excludes sibling branches. Git-backed files keep the tree inspectable.

title: After the meeting
subtitle: Follow the discussion. Ask during or after.
description: A Microsoft Teams preview that answers questions from captured live captions or completed transcripts, with an opt-in pilot for rolling updates and meeting-to-date summaries.
capabilities: Answer live-caption and completed-transcript questions with speaker and timestamp citations
Keep recent ended-session captions available while awaiting the Graph transcript
Produce opt-in rolling updates and meeting-to-date summaries of supported topics, decisions, actions, risks, and open questions
note: Preview, not production-ready. Summaries are disabled by default; the November 10 two-meeting pilot was accepted, but a later summary omitted a corrected value. Long-meeting, restart, and multi-speaker accuracy remain separate checks. Single-instance JSON storage still lacks production data controls; use non-sensitive test meetings only.
problem: Following decisions during a meeting and finding answers afterward should not require manually searching every caption or transcript.
how: An optional ACS browser participant captures finalized live captions; Meeting Copilot answers actual chat mentions. After a session ends, it prefers its completed Graph transcript, otherwise recent ended-session captions. Opt-in summaries post new-caption updates and a condensed meeting-so-far view, using versioned packaged instructions or optional private Blob instructions. Silent windows make no summary model call.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. This is an adaptation of a Microsoft Teams sample with a documented transcript-question-answering workflow and deployment configuration. Microsoft services and the original sample are dependencies, not original components claimed by this portfolio.

title: A token stays with the broker
subtitle: An agent can use a tool without holding the user’s token.
description: A proof of concept that puts OAuth credential handling in Azure API Management so a Foundry agent can call a narrow Microsoft Graph tool without receiving the user’s access token.
capabilities: APIM validates a managed-identity caller before tool use
Credential Manager owns the consent, token cache, and refresh
A public explainer and template document the bounded integration
note: The README reports runtime and negative-path checks for one bounded approach. Per-user isolation / per-user OAuth passthrough is not proven. This portfolio did not redeploy the infrastructure or independently repeat those provider checks. No tenant screenshots or identifiers are reproduced.
problem: Giving an agent a user’s token expands the consequences of a leak. A narrow broker can keep the credential boundary separate from the model.
how: The Foundry agent authenticates to APIM with a managed identity. APIM validates the caller, obtains a token from Credential Manager, calls Graph, and returns the tool result rather than the credential.
contribution: Individual role unverified: the approved public sources describe the artifact, not Jorge’s specific changes. The public artifact includes an architectural walkthrough, an interactive diagram, APIM integration work, and a reusable Bicep template. It documents both the chosen approach and the limits of what its reported checks establish.

title: Evidence-preserving document intelligence
subtitle: Keep the mark, its source and the decision together.
description: A PDF evidence pipeline routing native, scanned and hybrid pages into span-preserving decisions, review artifacts and a search-ingestion handoff. This sanitized narrative is not public code inspection.
capabilities: Route native, scanned and hybrid pages; reuse optional document-level Azure Layout
Join native geometry and detector evidence to original word spans, with deterministic confirmation and review
Emit enriched, clean and provenance views plus sidecar, review queue and search-ingestion handoff
note: Private implementation; no fresh execution. The documented demo uses the real orchestrator with mocked cloud and detector responses, not accuracy or cloud acceptance. The scanned path may send the full PDF to cloud; page-local processing is not Azure response streaming. Human review remains necessary; confidence is not calibrated probability by default. Redistribution requires separate review.
problem: Flattening a PDF can erase whether a crossed-out phrase was confirmed or ambiguous, where it appeared, and why text was changed. Repeated phrases make global replacement unsafe.
how: Route each page; collect native annotation/vector geometry evidence or reuse one optional document-level Azure Layout response for scanned detection. Normalize polygons, join original word spans spatially, resolve confirmed versus review decisions deterministically, then emit enriched/clean/provenance outputs, sidecar and search-ingestion records.
contribution: Individual role unverified; this narrative does not establish sole authorship. The reviewed implementation combines page routing, evidence joins, deterministic resolution and inspectable artifacts. PyMuPDF, Azure Layout and optional detector dependencies are not claimed as original components. Only this separately authored sanitized narrative is public; code redistribution is a separate gate.

title: Diagnosing custom-model authentication
subtitle: Observe the client contract before changing the gateway gate.
description: A BYOK integration diagnostic using an isolated endpoint to observe authentication metadata, then validate the contract at Azure API Management and clean up. This sanitized narrative is not public code inspection.
capabilities: Use disposable dummy credentials and bounded metadata-only observation on an isolated endpoint
Validate the expected client contract at the gateway, strip incoming credentials and separate backend identity
Restore client routing, remove diagnostic configuration and explicitly review retention and access
note: Historical guide claims, not fresh execution or current universal client behavior. No model calls, gateway changes or deployments were performed. Never echo, log or forward credential values. Disposable diagnostics need bounded access/lifetime; isolation or an idle response is not a production safety guarantee. Private source stays unlinked; redistribution requires separate review.
problem: A blank configured key and a gateway expecting the wrong header can look like the same authentication failure. Guessing against a working route mixes discovery with enforcement.
how: Use a separate disposable endpoint with dummy credentials, static mock responses and allowlisted presence/scheme metadata only. The historical guide reports Authorization/Bearer. Validate with a secret-store-backed gateway value before routing, strip the incoming credential before separate managed-identity backend authentication, then restore and clean up.
contribution: Individual role unverified; the evidence does not establish sole authorship. This separately authored narrative explains a bounded diagnostic and gateway-validation method using existing platform capabilities. Historical gateway-console, HTTP and client retests are reported by the private guide, not independently rerun. No private guide, policies, screenshots or operational configuration are published.

title: Drawing a conversation
subtitle: Preserve the drawing. Keep its meaning open to question.
description: A single-owner drawing-conversation prototype that separates exact captured marks, a tentative model-authored reply, and the human interpretation of that reply.
capabilities: Capture and replay stroke geometry and timing without replacing archived originals
Require contextual consent before saving a drawing and requesting a model reply
Store a first reading before revealing the reply intention, then compare manually
note: Private prototype, not a public app. Reply timing is synthetic; comparison is manual, not an accuracy score. No Apple Digital Touch compatibility, native messaging integration, shared-meaning certification or consistent speed improvement is claimed. Source inspection only; no fresh execution. Private source release is a separate permission gate.
problem: A drawing can carry rhythm, hesitation and shape, yet still mean different things to its sender and receiver. A convincing reply is not evidence that both understood the same message.
how: A browser captures strokes locally. Explicit consent saves the original before inference. The experimental path sends a rendered image with geometry and timing, records a reply intention before a second model stage draws, and withholds the intention until the person stores a first reading.
contribution: Individual role unverified. The reviewed prototype connects immutable drawing evidence, a drawings-first conversation UI, bounded two-stage inference and a human comparison workflow. Existing browser, database and model capabilities are dependencies, not components claimed as newly invented.

title: A soundtrack for the session
subtitle: Let the session change the music without confusing intent with playback.
description: A local Spotify-first control surface that turns bounded coding-session signals into deterministic playlist choices while keeping requests separate from observed playback.
capabilities: Select curated music crates using scene dimensions and user-owned constraints
Hold or disable adaptation independently of pausing music
Distinguish queued controls, acknowledgements, failures and observed playback
note: Loopback application, not a hosted service. Spotify Premium, authorization, an active Connect device and configured crates are prerequisites. Adaptation starts enabled in the reviewed runtime; hold or disable it explicitly. An activity acknowledgement is not proof of a song switch. Source inspection only; no fresh execution. Private source release is a separate permission gate.
problem: A coding session changes direction, but constant playlist switching can interrupt it. A second problem is trust: receiving a music-control command does not mean the requested playback happened.
how: Bounded labels, tags and numeric scene dimensions reach a local policy. Curated crates and hard preference filters determine eligible choices. Hold times, cooldowns and track boundaries limit switching. Spotify is the default backend, and playback mutations are checked against fresh observations.
contribution: Individual role unverified. The reviewed artifact combines a compact player, deterministic scene policy, Spotify authorization and explicit delivery-state handling. Spotify provides playback; the player is not an original audio engine or an official Spotify product.

title: Knowledge that earns its place
subtitle: Capture freely. Promote carefully. Keep the evidence close.
description: A file-based knowledge workflow that leaves one-off notes searchable while requiring recurring evidence and human approval before treating an idea as maintained knowledge.
capabilities: Separate unrestricted raw capture from recurrence-gated knowledge promotion
Build bounded read-only context packets with exact supporting evidence
Prepare reviewable proposals and record explicit decisions with their reasons
note: Private implementation, not a public notebook. Recurrence establishes eligibility, not truth. The packet builder does not call a model. Review recording does not itself promote a page, and no cognitive or retrieval-quality improvement is claimed. Source inspection only; no fresh execution. Private source release is a separate permission gate.
problem: A note written once can become a polished page before anyone decides it is durable. Repetition of the same event across files can also masquerade as independent support.
how: Raw notes remain discoverable without promotion. Candidate eligibility requires at least two independent source units spaced three or more calendar days apart, with event deduplication. An agent prepares evidence-backed changes for a human decision; a deterministic packet builder retrieves accepted knowledge with exact source evidence under a hard budget.
contribution: Individual role unverified. The reviewed engine combines recurrence checks, event-aware source handling, evidence-bounded retrieval and explicit review records on a portable Markdown substrate. Existing editors render links; no custom graph engine or autonomous preference-learning result is claimed.
